findings.finding: WB HTTP 403 is unconditionally mapped to SCOPE_MISSING. The selected /api/v1/seller-info method is documented as available to any token category, so 403 alone does not prove a missing scope; it may signal another authorization/provider condition. This overstates diagnostic certainty and can mislead platform UX.
findings.recommendation: Map WB 403 to CHECK_UNAVAILABLE unless WB documents a structured scope-specific error discriminator for this endpoint. Add fixtures for 403 with and without recognized structured discriminator.

findings.finding: Socket parent validation rejects world-writable directories but permits group-writable parents. A group-writable parent may permit another group member to race the pathname between bind/chmod/inode capture, depending on deployed group membership; this weakens the stated private-path ownership guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Require parent not group- or world-writable unless the exact trusted group and deployment ownership model are explicitly pinned; perform chmod and inode capture against a verified socket inode with race-resistant handling.

findings.finding: Seller response validation checks a minimum subset of company fields but accepts arbitrary additional/missing top-level and company fields. This is fail-closed for promotion when those minimum fields are absent and binding qualification is false, but it is not a strict complete expected schema as described in the review request.
findings.recommendation: Either call this a minimum schema guard, or validate documented required top-level/company fields while permitting documented optional fields. Keep promotion disabled absent binding qualification.
